brief.headline: Nothing has settled since Friday, so the page opens on a carried board for a third run - but the week's framing has changed underneath it: the Federal Reserve's own projections now point higher for longer, Hormuz transits are running at a third to a half of normal, and the analyst forecast spread on aluminium has widened to more than six hundred dollars a tonne.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: nothing on the exchange, and this run says so plainly. The London ring publishes today's official at 13:20 London; this page compiled at 03:35 London. The complete, published 18-September official is therefore carried for a THIRD consecutive run after a shut Saturday and Sunday - cash $3,285.00, three-month $3,282.00, stock 242,600 tonnes with a reported change of zero, backwardation $3.00. Verified cache-busted in both Westmetall language versions and against the per-metal daily table, which shows no row after 18-September. Three days without a ring is the longest gap this page has carried.

WHAT IS NEW IS MACRO, NOT PHYSICAL. Analysis published 20-September sets out the Federal Open Market Committee's updated projections behind the 16-September increase to 3.75-4.00%: the median expected 2026 federal funds rate was revised from 3.8% to 4.1%, with 3.9% for 2027 and 3.6% for 2028, and two meetings left this year. That converts a single hike into a confirmed higher-for-longer path, which is the channel that has been visibly biting this page's curve rather than its price.

AND THE SHIPPING PICTURE GOT WORSE, NOT BETTER. The same reporting puts daily commodity vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal 12-18, citing Reuters tracking, and records a tanker struck by a projectile 16 nautical miles north-east of Khasab, Oman on 18-September. That sits directly against the restart-and-normalisation story the producer panel has been telling, and the two cannot both be fully right - the disagreement is shown here rather than resolved.

WHAT TO WATCH: today's 13:20 London official, and it is the same binary question this page set on Friday - does the $3.00 cash-to-three-month spread RE-WIDEN beyond $15.00, HOLD near flat, or CROSS into contango? Watch the stock line with equal weight: a second consecutive zero, or a genuine build, would confirm the draw has ended rather than paused. Then the October FOMC, and the Q4 Japanese premium settlement now under two weeks away with a pending range of $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t.

lme.commentary: THERE IS NO NEW BOARD YET TODAY, AND THE RIGHT RESPONSE IS TO SAY SO PLAINLY RATHER THAN RE-NARRATE FRIDAY AS IF IT HAD JUST HAPPENED. Both Westmetall language overviews were re-requested cache-busted this morning and agree line for line across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings; more decisively, the aluminium per-metal daily table shows NO ROW AFTER 18-SEPTEMBER, which is what distinguishes a complete board from a cached one. No discrepancy was found in either direction. WHAT THE CARRIED BOARD STILL SAYS, AND HAS NOW SAID FOR THREE RUNS WITHOUT BEING TESTED, IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING ON THIS PAGE. Spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction, which removes the positioning-artefact explanation. THE CROSS-METAL CONTROL STILL POINTS THE OTHER WAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS READ AS ALUMINIUM-SPECIFIC RATHER THAN MACRO: on that identical ring copper flipped from an $8.50 CONTANGO into a $14.00 BACKWARDATION while drawing 800 tonnes, and zinc sits in a $97.00 backwardation with cash at $4,010.00 against three-month $3,913.00. A board where three metals tightened their fronts and aluminium's went flat is not describing a dollar event or a rates event; it is describing something specific to aluminium availability. drivers.text: THE EXCHANGE HAS STOPPED PAYING FOR IMMEDIACY, AND THE NEGOTIATION HAS HAD A WHOLE WEEKEND TO ABSORB THAT — On the 18-September LME official the cash-to-three-month backwardation collapsed from $18.50 to $3.00, an 84% erosion in one session and the fourth consecutive narrowing, while three-month moved only $3.00. That spread has now stood at three dollars through Saturday and Sunday with no opportunity to re-widen, because there is no ring. A backwardation is the physical market paying to have metal now; at $3.00 it is paying almost nothing. For a quarterly premium negotiation this is the cleanest published argument a buyer has, and unlike a view it carries a date and a settlement price. WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT IS EQUALLY PUBLISHED: a re-widening beyond $15.00 on Monday's official.

Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah remains a partial restart at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return to previous output guided for early 2027. NEW AND DATED THIS RUN: analysis published 20-September on SMM data reports China's aluminium billet stocks easing to 152,500 tonnes on 17-September from a four-year seasonal high of 157,500 tonnes on 14-September, with billet processing fees rebounding across Foshan, Wuxi and Nanchang - two of them from BELOW-COST territory - after the SMM A00 spot price fell about RMB 380/mt over the week. A downstream that only buys when the price falls is not a downstream that validates a record premium.

The quarterly split is the material part - Q2-2026 revenue RMB 60.61bn, DOWN 1.9% y/y, and Q2 attributable net profit RMB 3.53bn, DOWN 26.2% y/y, against a Q1 that had risen 56.35%. THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA PRODUCER EARNED MATERIALLY LESS IN A QUARTER WHEN THE LME CASH AVERAGE WAS ABOVE $3,200, AND THAT IS THE SIGNAL. A 26% year-on-year fall in Q2 attributable profit on flat-to-lower revenue points to margin compression rather than volume weakness, and it is consistent with the Chinese alumina spot picture carried on this board - SMM's Shandong index down toward 2,600 RMB/t with national capacity utilisation rising and trader inventories building. For a reader of the seaborne market the implication runs both ways: weaker Chinese alumina margins are disinflationary for the smelter cost basket globally, but a large integrated producer earning less at a high metal price also argues that the cost curve has moved up underneath everyone. The shares fell around 3% on the release. earnings.note: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds. THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

Added to this board and to the earnings-history panel this run as the designated progressive backfill. NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN CHURNED DAILY, AND THIS RUN IS A MATERIAL-CHANGE REVIEW RATHER THAN A CALENDAR ONE. TWO THINGS TRIGGERED IT. FIRST, THE HORMUZ CORRIDOR: dated 07-September reporting has Iran describing an arrangement with Oman to manage Strait shipping as days away, following a temporary route agreed in late August - the first documented de-escalation path in this conflict, though nothing is signed and the waterway has not reopened. SECOND, THE ALUMINA CORRIDOR: dated 12-September evidence shows Asia exporting 7.05 Mt of alumina in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year, with India swinging to a 1.72 Mt trade surplus on exports up 51.3% and imports down 34.9%. THE CHINA-TO-WEST SEMIS CORRIDOR IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISM RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE. REVIEW NOTE, 19-SEPTEMBER: this panel is reviewed monthly or on material change, not refreshed daily. It was reviewed this run and NO CORRIDOR HAS BEEN CHANGED. One development was weighed and rejected as insufficient: commodity reporting captured 18-September indicates a PARTIAL easing of Strait of Hormuz transit, with satellite imagery suggesting about 2.8 million barrels a day of Saudi crude moved through over six days against roughly 700,000 in August, alongside roughly 60 million barrels routed outside the strait via ship-to-ship transfer. That is crude, not metal, and the same reporting records only four commodity vessels detected transiting on the Thursday. A corridor is not re-rated on an adjacent commodity's partial recovery; it is re-rated when metal flow evidence prints. Aluminium Bahrain's confirmed routing via Jeddah and Sohar - around rather than through Hormuz - is consistent with the corridor remaining impaired.

THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no agreement is signed. THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS EVIDENTIAL CATEGORY, FROM UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR TO DATED MULTI-OUTLET REPORTING, AND THAT IS WHY THE CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED WHILE THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS NOT DECLARED REPAIRED. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON - THE FIRST NEW EXCHANGE INFORMATION IN FOUR DAYS AND THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. There has been no ring since Friday, so this settlement carries the whole weekend's positioning in one print. THE QUESTION IS BINARY AND WAS STATED IN ADVANCE ON FRIDAY: does the cash-to-three-month spread RE-WIDEN beyond $15.00, HOLD near flat, or CROSS into outright CONTANGO? A re-widening restores the tightness case and would lift the bull scenario back toward 30%. A crossing into contango would be the first session this cycle on which the exchange stops paying for immediacy at all, and would raise the bear case. Watch the stock line with equal attention: a second consecutive zero, or a genuine BUILD, would confirm the drawdown has ended rather than paused.

THE 3,261 LEVEL FACES ITS FIRST POST-WEEKEND TEST. Three-month closed the week at $3,282.00, $21.00 above it, and has settled above it every session since 15-September. Weekend gaps are precisely where levels that held on momentum get retested on fresh positioning, and this level has now gone three days without being examined. A daily settlement below 3,261 is the published condition for raising the bear scenario, and on the weekly Elliott count it is the level the position-degree structure turns on. The stated SMM range for this week is $3,200-3,350/t, which contains both the level and Friday's close.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED - A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. Nothing has published into this window, so roughly a fifth of the smelter cash-cost stack is carried on marks about a month old. When it prints, the direction is signposted by a Brent that fell three consecutive sessions to about $103.21 on 18-September - but signposted is not settled, and this page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists.

WHETHER XINJIANG'S OUTBOUND RAIL BACKLOG BEGINS TO CLEAR - THE MOST DIRECT TEST OF WHETHER CHINA'S 63,000-TONNE WEEKLY DRAW WAS TIGHTNESS OR DELAY. The province runs at 99.97% utilisation with essentially no idle buffer and hauls 4,000-5,000 km to the southeastern ports at a stated RMB 400-600/t transport premium, so a rail constraint suppresses warehouse arrivals almost immediately. The reversal mechanism is known: delayed ingots do not trickle back, they arrive in bulk, and a cleared bottleneck in late December 2025 is cited as the precedent for a sharp stock spike. Watch also whether the unquantified Guangxi billet maintenance curtailments acquire a tonnage.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn of imports in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. This is a regional-delivered-price event, not an LME event: it moves US premiums and trade routing rather than the exchange price. Public forecasting already has the US Midwest premium averaging its highest-ever level in 2026 on the 50% headline rate.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside. The range is unchanged for a seventh consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP GAINED A FOURTH BUYER-SIDE ARGUMENT THIS RUN: alongside the collapsed exchange backwardation, Alba's quantified 1.3 Mt restart and a Chinese downstream that only bought when spot fell RMB 380/mt, a billet overhang of about 142,000 tonnes that eased by only 500 tonnes in a week is evidence that demand at the record level is simply not there.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND. Dated analysis identifies pre-holiday restocking as one of two drivers of the 63,000-tonne weekly ingot destock and states plainly that holiday demand is temporary by definition. The test is explicit: STRONG post-holiday operating rates that absorb the returning metal would mean the tightness was genuine; a MUTED return with inventory rebuilding would confirm it was seasonal and logistics-driven. A comparable early-2025 cycle is cited with inventory peaking at 850,000-900,000 tonnes once the restocking catalyst expired. Note the reporting lag: operating-rate surveys arrive one to two weeks after the price move.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND IT MATTERS MORE THIS RUN THAN LAST. With the dot plot now revised to a 4.1% median for 2026 against 3.8% in June, and two meetings left in October and December, the projections imply at least one further increase before year-end. The observed pass-through to aluminium so far is small - a combined -0.21% on three-month across the two settlements containing the September decision - but carry acts on the curve rather than the price, and the curve is exactly where this page's central question sits. A hold in October would remove the cleanest bearish argument against the backwardation re-widening.

risks.text: THE FEDERAL RESERVE IS NO LONGER JUST A STANDING HEADWIND - THE PATH ITSELF WAS REVISED UPWARD, AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP. The Committee raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously at 12-0, the first increase since July 2023. WHAT IS NEW THIS RUN IS THE PROJECTION PATH BEHIND IT: the median 2026 federal funds expectation was lifted from 3.8% in June to 4.1%, with 3.9% for 2027 and 3.6% for 2028, and two meetings remain on the 2026 calendar. That is not a technical tweak; it makes higher-for-longer the published central case through at least mid-2027, and it removes a dovish pivot as near-term support. THE CHANNEL THAT BITES HERE IS CARRY, NOT THE DOLLAR. Across the two settlements containing the decision aluminium three-month moved a combined -0.21% and the currency channel did essentially nothing; but real ten-year yields are reported at 4.3-4.4% and this page carries a nominal ten-year at 4.997%. A financing cost at that level is structurally hostile to a backwardation, because nobody is paid enough to hold the stock a backwardation exists to attract. The collapsed $3.00 spread and the yield level are consistent with each other, which is the most useful cross-check on this page today.

THE GULF SUPPLY PICTURE IS NOW GENUINELY CONTESTED IN PUBLIC AND THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT BECAUSE THE NEW EVIDENCE POINTS BOTH WAYS AT ONCE. On the unwinding side, the dated, named, CEO-sourced position stands: Aluminium Bahrain is running at about 1.3 million tonnes annualised on Lines 4, 5 and 6, roughly 80% of a pre-war 1,623 kt plant, with exports via Jeddah and Sohar, and Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah remains a partial restart at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return to previous output guided for early 2027. ON THE OTHER SIDE, AND THIS IS NEW THIS RUN, CRU GROUP IS REPORTED AS HOLDING THAT GULF PRODUCTION IS DOWN AROUND 25% YEAR ON YEAR on war-induced cuts and energy-supply disruption. Both cannot be fully right, and this page will not quietly pick the one that fits its narrative. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS A WIDER RANGE RATHER THAN A DIRECTION: the published deficit spread runs 300,000-500,000 tonnes in the base case against up to 1.4 million tonnes in the bull case, and that spread is the honest encoding of the disagreement. The LEVEL of this risk is unchanged and high; only the confidence in the direction has fallen.

TARIFF POLICY REMAINS THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE AND NOTHING ESCALATED - HELD AT FLAT. The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and UNCHANGED at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. The 08-September White House annex adding 50% to previously exempt downstream lines - producing a combined levy of up to 100% on some products - and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn of imports both remain in force but are twelve days old. NO NEW TARIFF ACTION PRINTED INTO THIS WINDOW. The next dated step is a US vehicle and dairy import ban on 29-September. At $3,285.00 cash the 50% leg alone is about $1,642.50/t, which is why US premiums on this page must be read as policy numbers.

THE COST FLOOR IS FLAT TO FALLING ON THE ENERGY LINES AND SIMPLY ABSENT ON THE CARBON LINES - HELD AT FLAT, AND THE DATA GAP IS NOW THE LARGER HALF OF THIS RISK. Brent fell for a third consecutive session to about $103.87 with reporting attributing it to easing Saudi supply risk rather than weak demand, and coal eased 0.45% to 144.00; working the other way, European gas TTF rose to about EUR 79.52 and is the only clearly rising energy line, which matters specifically for Alunorte's TEMPORARY gas-supplier terminal-access agreement and Qatalum's reduced-gas curtailment. THE CARBON COMPLEX IS THE REAL GAP: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke normally settle around the 17th-18th of the month and NO NEW PUBLIC SETTLEMENT HAS PRINTED, so roughly a fifth of cash cost is carried on marks about a month old. That is a data risk as much as a price risk and it is declared rather than smoothed over.

THE BACKWARDATION HAS COLLAPSED RATHER THAN MERELY ERODED, HAS NOW STOOD UNTESTED FOR THREE CALENDAR DAYS, AND IS RESOLVED IN HOURS - IMPACT HELD AT HIGH, TREND HELD AT FLAT. The four-run sequence is $21.00, $18.50, $18.50, $3.00 - an 84% fall in a single session and the fourth consecutive narrowing, leaving the curve within three dollars of flat. This page named the pattern three runs ago when it was still arguably noise and stated the test in advance; the test resolved against the tightness case. Two features made that print hard to dismiss: spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction, removing the positioning-artefact explanation, and the LME stock draw stopped dead at exactly zero on the same session. WHY THE TREND IS FLAT AND NOT UP: there has been no ring since, so the risk has neither intensified nor receded - it is frozen, and marking a frozen risk as rising would be manufacturing information. WHAT TURNS IT DOWN IS PUBLISHED AND SPECIFIC: a re-widening beyond $15.00 on a settled official. What makes it worse is a crossing into outright CONTANGO. TODAY'S 13:20 LONDON OFFICIAL RESOLVES IT, and the rate path revised this run argues, weakly, against the re-widening case.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN HAS STOPPED AND HAS NOT RESUMED, BECAUSE IT HAS HAD NO OPPORTUNITY TO - HELD AT FLAT. The last reported change was EXACTLY ZERO and the line is carried unchanged at 242,600 tonnes, the only flat session in the fifteen-session window and the session immediately after the largest draw of that window. A flat print is NOT a build and this page will not call it one; the level remains close to multi-decade lows and about 8,600 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215. But the daily confirmation that visible tightness is still being consumed has gone, and it went on the same session the backwardation collapsed. The chart floor stays at 235,000 with 7,600 tonnes of headroom and is re-checked every run.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS VISIBLE, DATED AND QUANTIFIED AT ITS LARGEST LINE - BUT THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT BECAUSE NO NEW RESTART EVIDENCE PRINTED. The publicly reported list carries Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 Mt annualised against a 1,623 kt plant; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 t; Slovalco restarting the first 75,000 t of 175,000 t guided for Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals with a first potline guided before end-2026 for about 75,000 t, with public reporting attributing the investment case to the 50% US tariff; and EGA's DX+ Ultra licence to NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion. Restarts are slow and none of this lands this quarter, which is why it is Medium and Medium. Nothing was added over the weekend.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS MARKED BACK TO FLAT THIS RUN, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE SAME SOURCE THAT SUPPLIED YESTERDAY'S IMPROVEMENT ALSO SUPPLIES THE CONTRADICTION. The improvement is real and dated: billet stocks eased to 152,500 tonnes on 17-September from a four-year seasonal high of 157,500 tonnes on 14-September, warehouse withdrawals rose 2,800 tonnes on the week to 38,900 tonnes, processing fees rebounded across Foshan, Wuxi and Nanchang with two hubs climbing out of below-cost territory, and national social inventory fell 63,000 tonnes to below 800,000 tonnes for the first time this cycle. BUT THE TWO NUMBERS THAT TEST WHETHER THAT IS DEMAND BOTH FAILED: the roughly 142,000-tonne billet overhang eased by only 500 tonnes in the week, and the share of liquid aluminium usage FELL 0.02 percentage points on select downstream curtailments. If consumption were accelerating, liquid usage would rise. ADD THE NAMED DRIVERS - a Xinjiang outbound rail bottleneck and pre-holiday restocking, both of which reverse by design - and the arrow cannot honestly stay down. This is a risk paused, not a risk receding.

A PREMIUM PANEL WHERE EVERY ROW HAS BEEN CARRIED FOR THREE CONSECUTIVE RUNS IS A DATA RISK IN ITS OWN RIGHT - HELD AT FLAT, BUT THE CARRY IS NOW LONG ENOUGH TO NAME. No price-reporting agency published over the weekend and none publishes before the London ring on a Monday, so no row in the premium panel CAN have moved since Friday, and every row is carried at its last dated public mark with the as-of date stated. The oldest material carry is the CIF Japan spot indication at $370/t. The settled Q3 Japanese benchmark of $395/t is not stale - a quarterly benchmark is fixed until the quarter turns - but it is increasingly disconnected from dated September spot reporting of roughly $320-380/t. THE RISK THIS CREATES IS SPECIFIC AND NOW UNDER TWO WEEKS OUT: the Q4 settlement, due late September or early October, could reset 22-29% lower in a single print, and a reader looking only at the panel would see no warning in the numbers themselves. The warning is written here instead. Working the other way, public forecasting has the US Midwest premium averaging its HIGHEST-EVER level in 2026 on the 50% Section 232 rate - so the two ends of the premium complex are diverging, not moving together.

STRAIT OF HORMUZ SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS ADDED AS A RISK IN ITS OWN RIGHT THIS RUN, WITH THE TREND SET TO UP ON DATED EVIDENCE. Reuters tracking cited in analysis published 20-September puts daily commodity vessel transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a ten-day moving average that normally runs 12-18 - a third to a half of normal, sustained over more than a fortnight. A tanker was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile 16 nautical miles north-east of Khasab, Oman on 18-September and caught fire; strikes also hit a Saudi oil pipeline and a regional shipping-security conference in Oman was rescheduled. WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE RISK RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE TO GULF SUPPLY: a lane constraint raises the delivered cost of metal that was produced perfectly normally, and it raises freight and war-risk surcharges for cargoes that never touch a damaged smelter. IT IS ALSO THE SINGLE CLEANEST EXPLANATION AVAILABLE FOR WHY CRU AND THE RESTART REPORTING DISAGREE. THE ATTRIBUTION OF THE STRIKE IS UNCONFIRMED and the transit counts are the harder half of the claim; the risk is marked up on the counts, not on the projectile.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
